question: A pituitary macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm from below characteristically produces a bitemporal hemianopia because the crossing nasal fibres (representing the temporal visual field) are compressed at the chiasm.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The optic chiasm decussation is the key anatomical fact: nasal retinal fibres (= temporal visual field) cross; temporal fibres (= nasal visual field) do not. Chiasmal compression = bitemporal hemianopia. This is the pathognomonic field defect of a pituitary tumour.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The nasal fibres from each retina (representing the temporal visual field of each eye) cross at the chiasm. Compression of the chiasm from below (e.g., by a pituitary adenoma) preferentially affects these crossing fibres, producing bitemporal hemianopia — loss of the outer (temporal) half of vision in both eyes.
